rationale: The TiDB obligation is the concrete user-variable state instance of retry rollback closure.
The module profile names the mutation, retry acceptance, rollback, and consumer owners.
The oracle observes both terminal error suppression and persistent row-image drift.
The unique-key race turns the state leak into a natural user-visible conflict.
The schedule separates error altitude, idempotence, natural reachability, and exact repair.
The bounded six-arm schedule directly executes the retry side-effect closure obligation.
The late conflict triggers re-entry after the unrestored user-variable mutation.
The GREEN controls prove that altitude and next-attempt input dependence select the RED.
